sentences.text: Thalattoarchon was a large predatory ichthyosaur that lived in North America during the Middle Triassic period.
This animal possessed large teeth with two cutting edges that could reach up to 12 cm in length, alongside elongated eye sockets reaching up to 29 cm, each containing a scleral ring.
Despite incomplete fossils, the animal is estimated to have had at least 60 presacral vertebrae.
The original describing team estimated Thalattoarchon to be over 8.6 meters long, making it a particularly large ichthyosaur.
Thalattoarchon spent its entire life in the water and exhibited reduced bone ossification adapted to marine existence.
In 2021, researchers proposed that Thalattoarchon could have reached a body mass of 4.3 metric tons.
Thalattoarchon lived four million years after the first appearance of ichthyosaurs in the Early Triassic, making it the first marine reptile to become a superpredator.
The existence of Thalattoarchon suggests that marine ecosystems recovered faster than terrestrial ones after the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.
Thalattoarchon was described in 2013 based on a single partial skeleton found in Nevada, discovered in 1997 by paleontologist Jim Holstein in the Augusta Mountains.

The fossils were completely exhumed in 2008 with support from the National Geographic Society after three weeks of work, and the type species Thalattoarchon saurophagis was formally described in 2013.
In 2013, the specimen was designated the holotype for the new species Thalattoarchon saurophagis by a team including Nadia B. Fröbisch and Olivier Rieppel.
Thalattoarchon is known from a single skeleton consisting of a partial skull, vertebrae, hip bones, and parts of the hind flippers.
Thalattoarchon was an active animal with a high metabolic rate that allowed it to maintain its body temperature.
Thalattoarchon is recognized as an apex predator due to its large, robust head and bicarinate cutting teeth, and due to these adaptations, it likely did not feed on ammonites, squid, or fish.
Thalattoarchon is considered the oldest known aquatic megapredator tetrapod in the fossil record.
Thalattoarchon lived eight million years after the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, preceding the first appearance of terrestrial superpredators after the Carnian Pluvial Event in the Late Triassic.
Thalattoarchon was one of the most abundant marine reptiles found in the Fossil Hill Member.

The classification of Thalattoarchon is debated, with it being placed either in the clade Merriamosauria or the basal family Cymbospondylidae, though in 2021, Sander and colleagues reclassified Thalattoarchon within the Merriamosauria as the sister taxon to the Shastasauridae.
Thalattoarchon belongs to the parent group Merriamosauria and is classified in the class Reptilia.
The fossils date to approximately 244.6 million years ago, corresponding to the beginning of the late Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
It is debated whether Thalattoarchon hunted Cymbospondylus using a pack-hunting strategy, as this behavior is not reported in the fossil record.
Researchers suggest Thalattoarchon may have fed only on smaller animals, living or dead, similar to a great white shark.
